clue.text: Labourer's assistant could be so devious

definitions.meaning: an ..., or subordinate helper, is someone working below a skilled labourer
devious means sly or done secretly

explanation.surface: A workman's helper is suspected of being shifty.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the first definition as two words, under and hand: a hand (worker) placed under another.
explanation.definitionFit: Underhand dealings are sly and secret, the same as devious ones.

clue.text: Stimulant blows head off drinker!

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word for a drinker is knocked away, as a head is blown off

parts.note: a supper is one who sups, i.e. drinks

explanation.surface: A boozer gets his head blown off by a stimulant, a lurid tabloid headline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drinker' is not a noun for a toper here but SUPPER, one who sups.
explanation.definitionFit: An upper is slang for a stimulant drug such as amphetamine.

clue.text: Working men in Black Country

indicators.note: the shuffled letters are placed inside the word for black

parts.note: black means dark

indicators.note: working suggests the letters of men being set in motion and rearranged

explanation.surface: Labourers employed in the Black Country, the industrial West Midlands of England.
explanation.walkthrough: The Black Country is an industrial area around Birmingham, but the phrase splits: 'Black' is wordplay and 'Country' alone defines. 'Working' is the anagram signal, and 'in' puts the result inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Denmark is a Scandinavian nation, an example of a country.

clue.text: Very last of troupe to quit demonstration

indicators.note: the final letter of troupe leaves the word for very

parts.note: really means very, as in really good

indicators.note: the very last letter of troupe is the one taken

explanation.surface: The final member of a theatrical company walks out of a protest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Very' does double duty in the surface as 'very last', but it is the leaf REALLY; 'last of troupe' is E, which 'to quit' removes.
explanation.definitionFit: A rally is a mass meeting held in protest or support, a demonstration.

clue.text: Old reports about Ursula's first bloomers

indicators.note: the old reports are wrapped about the chosen letter

parts.note: annals are historical records, reports of years gone by

indicators.note: first picks only the opening letter of Ursula

explanation.surface: Historic accounts of Ursula's underwear, the knickers called bloomers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomers' looks like old-fashioned knickers but means plants that flower; ANNALS goes round U.
explanation.definitionFit: Annuals are plants that flower and die within a year, so they are bloomers.

clue.text: Lee proved to be sporting photographer's solution

indicators.note: sporting suggests the letters playing about and so being rearranged

explanation.surface: A man called Lee showed himself a good sport about something a photographer needed.
explanation.definitionFit: Developer is the chemical solution used to bring out the image on exposed film.

clue.text: Believe house comes with vacant grounds

indicators.note: vacant means the inside of the word for grounds is emptied, leaving its ends

parts.note: land means grounds, as in an estate's land

explanation.surface: Someone trusts that a house is being sold with empty grounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vacant' empties LAND of its middle AN, leaving LD.
explanation.definitionFit: To hold a view is to believe it, as in holding that something is true.

clue.text: Colt might be secured by this composer, on reflection

definitions.text: Colt might be secured by this

parts.note: Gustav Holst was the English composer of The Planets

indicators.note: on reflection the short word for on is seen as in a mirror, read backwards

parts.note: re means on, concerning

explanation.surface: A young horse might be calmed by a composer, thinking it over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Colt' suggests a young horse but is the revolver; 'on reflection' turns RE into ER.
explanation.definitionFit: A holster is a leather case for a handgun, and Colt is a famous make of revolver.

clue.text: One-time superior European city with lake by old road

parts.note: Liège is a city in Belgium
L is the abbreviation for lake on maps

explanation.surface: A former boss lives in a continental city beside a lake and an ancient highway.
explanation.definitionFit: A liege lord was a feudal master owed allegiance by vassals, a superior of former times.

clue.text: Switching on Apple with new version of office

indicators.note: switching signals the letters changing places with one another

explanation.surface: Turning on an Apple computer running a new release of Microsoft Office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'office' looks like the software suite, but it is a workplace layout.
explanation.definitionFit: An open-plan office has no internal walls, one style or kind of workplace.

clue.text: Hail lovely ground

indicators.note: ground means crushed or milled, so the letters are broken up and reformed

explanation.surface: Hailstones on a beautiful football pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: A volley is a hail, a rapid shower of missiles such as bullets or arrows.

clue.text: Wretched old Tory right-wingers holding back

indicators.note: holding means the picked letters contain the word for back
the right-hand wing of each of the words old and Tory is its last letter

parts.note: the rear is the back

explanation.surface: Miserable ex-Conservative hardliners resisting progress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right-wingers' looks political but takes the right-hand ends of 'old' and 'Tory', D and Y, which hold REAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Dreary means gloomy and dismal, so wretched in the sense of depressing.

clue.text: Excitedly anticipating a modest backing

parts.note: a flutter is a small bet, a modest backing of a horse

explanation.surface: Someone eagerly awaiting results after a small bet, a fair picture of a punter.
explanation.walkthrough: A flutter is British slang for a small bet, as on a horse race.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in a nervous, excited state of anticipation is to be all of a flutter.

clue.text: Dodge Row

definitions.meaning: a dodge is a scam or swindle
a row is a noisy din or uproar

explanation.surface: Reads like Dodge Row, the name of a street.
explanation.definitionFit: A racket is both an illegal money-making scheme and a loud noise.

clue.text: Warning: a large branch by our cartoonist

parts.note: L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
an arm is a branch, as of a river or an organisation
Steve Bell is a long-standing Guardian cartoonist, so 'ours' for this paper

explanation.surface: A cartoonist draws a large branch as a warning sign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'our cartoonist' means the Guardian's own, Steve Bell.
explanation.definitionFit: An alarm bell, literal or figurative, is a sign that something is wrong.

clue.text: Rigid principles for the running of public transport

definitions.meaning: ... in a figurative sense are fixed rules that allow no deviation

definitions.text: for the running of public transport
definitions.meaning: trams run along their rails, the lines a tram follows

explanation.surface: Strict rules governing how the buses and trains are run.
explanation.definitionFit: Tramlines are literally the rails trams run on, and figuratively inflexible guidelines.

clue.text: Lofty's 'prior use' rumpus

definitions.note: Lofty's stands for 'lofty is', the adjective with a link word

indicators.note: a rumpus is a commotion, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A man nicknamed Lofty causes a row over who used something first.
explanation.walkthrough: Lofty looks like a nickname, but it is an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Superior means haughty and condescending, the same as lofty.

clue.text: Place vessels around large plot

parts.note: to lay is to place, as in lay the table

indicators.note: the vessels are put around the letter for large

parts.note: pans are cooking vessels

explanation.surface: Arranging pots round a big garden plot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plot' looks like a patch of land but is the verb; L goes inside PANS.
explanation.definitionFit: To lay plans is to scheme in advance, the same as to plot.

clue.text: Exercise right to sit on panel — that's a crime

indicators.note: in a down answer, sitting on means being placed above the next piece

parts.note: PE is physical education, i.e. exercise
a jury is a panel of citizens

explanation.surface: A juror claims a right to serve, which turns out to be an offence.
explanation.definitionFit: Perjury, lying under oath, is a criminal offence.

clue.text: Start to smoke joint and smell clean hair

indicators.note: the start of smoke means its opening letter only

parts.note: a ham is a joint of meat
poo, or pooh, is the exclamation made at a bad smell

explanation.surface: Someone lights up a joint of cannabis and then washes the smell out of their hair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'joint' suggests cannabis but is a cut of meat.
explanation.definitionFit: To shampoo is to wash the hair with a soapy cleanser.

clue.text: Board's on edge?

definitions.note: Board's stands for 'board is', a verb meaning lodge

parts.note: re means on, concerning
a side is an edge

explanation.surface: Is a plank resting on its edge? A carpenter's question.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Board' is not a plank or committee but the verb, to lodge with someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To board somewhere is to live or lodge there, which is to reside.

clue.text: Mass association of king and clergy member shortly in church area?

indicators.note: the king and shortened clergyman are placed inside the church area

parts.note: a see is a bishop's diocese
R is the abbreviation for rex, king

indicators.note: shortly means the clergy member's title is cut short

parts.note: a vicar is a member of the clergy

explanation.surface: A link between a monarch and a cleric in some parish district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mass' looks like a quantity but is a church service; 'shortly' trims the clergy member and 'in' places the pieces inside the diocese.
explanation.definitionFit: Mass is a religious service, the celebration of the Eucharist.

clue.text: Dancing rumba without a singer for protection

indicators.note: dancing suggests the letters moving about into a new order
without means the letter a is left out

parts.note: Ella Fitzgerald was the great jazz singer

explanation.surface: A singer who dances a rumba without a partner, seeking protection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' drops the A from RUMBA, and 'Dancing' rearranges what is left, RUMB, to UMBR.
explanation.definitionFit: An umbrella is a cover or shield, figuratively any protecting agency.

clue.text: A zek or tsar with wings clipped, backing coup

indicators.note: backing means the letters run backwards
clipping the wings removes the outermost letters, leaving the inside of the words

explanation.surface: A Soviet labour-camp prisoner or a Russian emperor, both brought low, behind a putsch.
explanation.walkthrough: A zek is a Gulag prisoner. 'with wings clipped' trims the outer letters from 'A zek or tsar', A Z and AR, leaving EKORTS; 'backing' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: A stroke is a sudden brilliant act, a coup, as in a masterstroke.

clue.text: One leaves the old governor's band

indicators.note: leaves means the single letter departs from the governor's title

parts.note: a satrap was a provincial governor of ancient Persia
a means one

explanation.surface: Someone quits a former governor's musical group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'band' looks like a group of musicians but is a strip of material.
explanation.definitionFit: A strap is a strip of leather or fabric, a band.

clue.text: Sort of boomerang likely to lose line and deviate

indicators.note: to deviate is to stray from a course, so the letters stray into a new order
losing the line means one letter for line is dropped

explanation.surface: A thrown boomerang is likely to lose its line and veer off course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to lose' drops an L, leaving IKELY, which 'deviate' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A kylie is an Aboriginal Australian word for a type of boomerang or throwing stick.

clue.text: Soak vessel and put back

parts.note: to ret is to soak flax or hemp to soften it
an urn is a vessel

explanation.surface: Steep a pot in water, then replace it.
explanation.walkthrough: RET is a specialist word: soaking flax to loosen its fibres.
explanation.definitionFit: To return something is to give or put it back.

clue.text: Pence's 'thing'? Just a little bit

parts.note: an article is a thing or item

explanation.surface: Quoting a politician named Pence calling something just a little bit of a thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pence' suggests the US politician Mike Pence, but it is money.
explanation.definitionFit: A particle is a tiny fragment or minute amount.

clue.text: 'Earth', the artist said

indicators.note: said means the painter's name is spoken and its sound taken

parts.note: Paul Klee was a Swiss-German painter

explanation.surface: A painter names the planet or soil.
explanation.walkthrough: KLEE is pronounced 'clay'.
explanation.definitionFit: Clay is a heavy sticky soil, a kind of earth.

clue.text: That's how pie ceremony reveals a fine specimen

indicators.note: reveals means the letters are exposed inside the run of words

explanation.surface: A pie-judging ceremony is how a prize-winning pastry gets shown off.
explanation.definitionFit: A showpiece is an outstanding example displayed to show quality.
